declared: 2026-11-08, before the frozen rustc 1.98.0 oracle of these exact bytes and before any candidate run of these bytes. The shapes reduce the crate record that follows census 10's once `FnPtr` coherence is repaired (an analysis-only diagnostic census, obj/parallel/census-batch10/diagnostics/d1): "specialization parent capture has no unique child anchor" at core's `impl<I: DoubleEndedIterator> DoubleEndedIteratorRefSpec for &mut I` (iter/traits/double_ended.rs:498), which specializes `impl<I: DoubleEndedIterator + ?Sized> DoubleEndedIteratorRefSpec for &mut I`. Drafts of the double-ended, iterator, shared-reference, named-lifetime, concrete-referent, nominal-lifetime and static-reference shapes (obj/parallel/census-batch10/repro/spec-*.rs, different bytes) were run through the analysis-only candidate before this declaration, and only the static draft passed; none was run through rustc. Each outcome follows the rule read in the pinned rustc 1.98.0 sources (compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/traits/specialize/mod.rs `specializes`, which equates the specializing impl's trait reference with the parent's fresh instantiation, lifetimes included, and compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/impl_wf_check/min_specialization.rs): a parent's lifetime parameter is the child's corresponding header lifetime, so a lifetime that only appears in both headers does not prevent specialization, and adding `Sized` (a specialization trait) to a `?Sized` parent is permitted; min_specialization still rejects a parent argument that is `'static` where the parent is generic and a child that repeats a lifetime in the parent's arguments

double-ended-ref.rs.reason: core's shape (iter/traits/double_ended.rs:473 and 498): `impl<I: Back + ?Sized> BackSpec for &mut I` with a `default fn`, specialized by `impl<I: Back> BackSpec for &mut I`, where `BackSpec: Back: Iter` and `&mut I` implements both

shared-reference.rs.reason: the same pair over `&I` with a plain trait bound and no supertrait

named-lifetimes.rs.reason: the pair over `&'a mut I` and `&'b mut I` with differently named header lifetimes

concrete-referent.rs.reason: `impl<'a> Spec for &'a u8` specializing `impl<'a, I: ?Sized> Spec for &'a I`

nominal-lifetime.rs.reason: the pair over a nominal with a lifetime parameter, `Wrap<'a, I>`, the child adding `I: Sized`

static-reference.rs.reason: guard: both headers use `&'static I`, so no lifetime is specialized

static-specialization.rs.reason: opponent: `impl<I: ?Sized> Spec for &'static I` specializing `impl<'a, I: ?Sized> Spec for &'a I` specializes on `'static` (rejected by min_specialization)

repeated-lifetime.rs.reason: opponent: `impl<'b> Spec for &'b &'b u8` specializing `impl<'a, I: ?Sized> Spec for &'a I` repeats `'b` in the parent's arguments (rejected by min_specialization)
